component.name: Ward
component.summary: Private messaging on the open XMPP network

description.p: Ward is a modern XMPP (Jabber) client for Linux and the BSDs. Chats are end-to-end encrypted with OMEMO by default, and Ward talks to Conversations, Monal, Dino, Gajim and every other XMPP app on any server, including your own.

ul.li: Encrypted by default: OMEMO 2 and legacy OMEMO, with QR-code verification and clear trust decisions
Optional OpenPGP that shares keys with GPGMan and GnuPG
Markdown messages with code highlighting, tables, quotes, spoilers and task lists
Groups and channels: invites, moderation, roles, bookmarks and group settings
Replies, reactions, edits, deleting for everyone, read receipts and typing notifications
Files and images, encrypted when the chat is
Several accounts, message requests, blocking, full-text search and history from the server
Server administration for admins, an XML console and service discovery for developers
Adaptive: works on desktops, tablets and Linux phones

description.p: Create groups with a suggested room address and invite contacts from a searchable list. Reject group-service domains when joining, with a clear message. The AppImage now opens photos and videos with the desktop's default app on every desktop.
Choose Default (OMEMO) for legacy OMEMO, OMEMO 2, GPG/PGP or Off. Removing a device now deletes its published OMEMO bundles, and Remove inactive devices cleans up orphaned ones.

Back up and restore this device's OMEMO identity and sessions, and export OpenPGP public or secret keys, so reinstalling Ward or moving to another computer keeps the same encryption keys. Importing a device backup keeps its device ID, so contacts do not have to approve a new device.

Calls work with Conversations and Snikket, including desktop screen sharing and microphone/speaker selection. The AppImage and Flatpak bundle GtkSourceView data, libspelling and the OMEMO libraries, and the Flatpak uses GNOME 50.
The first release: encrypted chats and groups, Markdown, files, several accounts, OpenPGP with GPGMan keys, server administration, and packages for many Linux distributions and the BSDs.
